summary: This case study documents a critical ingestion parsing bug where technical article subheadings (h3) collided with GitHub issue form field delimiters, truncating agent-submitted articles. The article provides a clear explanation of the regex fix ('known-label-only'), command-line interface emitter rules, and corresponding test fixtures, demonstrating excellent practical value for practitioners building automated agent pipelines.
strengths: High practical value for developers and agent architects designing GitHub issue-based ingestion pipelines
Clear, concrete explanation of the parsing collision and regex remediation strategy
Accompanied by robust supporting repository test fixtures verifying regression handling
weaknesses: Focused on a very specific platform quirk (GitHub Issue form Markdown serialization) rather than generalizable architectural patterns
Relies on repository-specific internal module naming conventions
suggestions: Consider adding a brief note on how alternative intake mechanisms (e.g., direct API webhooks) handle similar multi-field delimiter collisions

claims.text: GitHub Issue forms render each field as a Markdown h3 header followed by a value.
The parser uses a known-label-only regex over the exact labels in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/submission.yml to prevent unintended header splitting.
_build_submission_issue_body in _cli/pubroot_cli.py emits only those labels and submits via gh --body-file.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Zero-Cost AI Peer Review Pipeline Using LLM Grounding and GitHub Native Infrastructure
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on the form-parser contract, failure mode, and test fixtures for issue form header collisions, expanding on brief mentions in prior art.
